title: Highest temperature in London on August 30?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Official forecasts from the UK Met Office indicate a maximum of 23°C for London on August 30, with afternoon temperatures reaching 21–22°C amid a mix of bright spells and scattered showers.** Southwesterly winds and variable cloud cover are expected to limit stronger heating, keeping values close to seasonal norms for late August.

Multiple model runs (including ECMWF guidance referenced in forecasts) support highs in the low-20s Celsius range, with minor differences arising from the exact timing and intensity of any showers versus clearer intervals. The tight split in market-implied odds between 22°C and 23°C reflects this narrow uncertainty band, as small shifts in insolation, wind strength, or precipitation could tip the daily maximum either way at official monitoring sites. Historical climatology for the period shows similar variability, reinforcing why traders see these two outcomes as the primary contenders. Updated model guidance and Met Office briefings remain the key near-term catalysts for any further shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models for Zhengzhou on August 30 show consensus highs near 29–31°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies with light northeasterly flow, keeping the leading market probabilities tightly clustered. Variable cloud cover modulates surface heating by reducing incoming solar radiation while limiting overnight radiative cooling, producing modest diurnal ranges around 23–24°C lows. Recent cooling from northerly advection and scattered shower potential in the region have suppressed extremes compared with mid-August peaks above 34°C, though model spreads in boundary-layer moisture and timing of any convective activity introduce enough uncertainty to support roughly equal implied odds for 29°C, 30°C, and 31°C. Updated runs from agencies like the China Meteorological Administration will clarify whether increased insolation or lingering cloudiness shifts the exact daily maximum.
